one-check-per-line.why: all 6 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 6

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

words-only.why: I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 stay within their words. Check 1 requires "exactly two error lines" with non-empty error text, which follows from "prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row". Check 6 rejects a pending workflow, which follows from "green". Check 4 breaks the criterion. Expect line 4 only asks for the package.json fields, no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests covering the listed cases. Check 4's PASS list adds "`npm test -w jsonl-lint` passes", and its FAIL rule ("FAIL if any of these is missing") applies to that item too. The words of line 4 don't require the tests to pass; that belongs to line 6, which covers root `npm test` and the workflow. This extra condition sits in PASS/FAIL instead of under Advisory, so the criterion is not met.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. Steps 1–5 of the builder brief create packages/jsonl-lint/. Commands that use those files run in step 6 or later: `npm install`, `npm ci && npm test` and running the bin by hand. `chmod +x` and `node --test` with test/*.test.js are valid. The verifier brief calls `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <path>`, which the PR adds. The `-e` one-liner in Check 3 is valid inside bash double quotes: `\"` becomes a quote and `\n` stays a JS escape. `npm test -w jsonl-lint` uses the workspace name. One gap: I only saw the root package.json scripts, not its `workspaces` field. The root test script uses `--workspaces` and a lock file exists, so I assumed workspaces are configured. `gh pr list --search "102 in:body"`, `gh pr view <n> --json body,headRefOid,statusCheckRollup`, `test -f` and `grep -n jsonl-lint README.md` are valid. I found no broken syntax and no missing files.

catches-traps.why: Item 1 holds: builder step 6 says "run `npm install` so that `package-lock.json` includes the new workspace (CI runs `npm ci`…)". Item 2 holds: step 5 says "replace the 'No tools yet' bullet". Item 4 holds: check 6 uses `gh pr view … body,headRefOid,statusCheckRollup` and needs the `test` workflow to show SUCCESS for headRefOid. Item 3 breaks. Check 4 runs `npm test -w jsonl-lint`, which runs the workspace directly, not through the root script. Check 6 only requires "local `npm test` exits 0". Neither reads the root run's test count or breaks lint() to see a failure. Because the root script uses --if-present, the root npm test could pass with the jsonl-lint tests skipped, and the verifier would not notice.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its expect line. None is stricter than its line. Check 1 asks only for the `<path>:<n>: ` prefix followed by "non-empty error text", with no exact wording. Check 2 asks only for "non-empty stderr" and exit 2. Check 3 checks the shape, not the message. Check 6 checks what the line itself asks for. No check sets branch-name rules, mutation tests or limits on which files the PR may touch. The shebang, file mode, lock file and CRLF checks are marked Advisory, so they do not decide PASS or FAIL. The behaviour lines are checked by running things: checks 1 and 2 run the bin on fixtures, check 3 imports the module and calls it, and check 4 runs `npm test` while looking at the tests. Only checks 4 and 5 read files directly, and those lines describe file contents. The builder brief's extras, such as `private` and `engines`, are build instructions, not PASS/FAIL conditions.
